definitions.explanation: A road-running relay in which each member of a team runs one leg and hands a sash to the next runner. It is one of Japan's most-watched sports, run by schools, universities, and companies, and the New Year's university races are national television events.

⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大学|だいがく}→大学：00608_daigaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{駅伝|えきでん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出場|しゅつじょう}した→出場する：20348_shutsujousuru⟧。
examples.english: My older brother competed in the university ekiden.

examples.japanese: {駅伝|えきでん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{個人|こじん}→個人：02758_kojin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{速|はや}さ→速さ：28072_hayasa⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧、たすき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つなぐ⟦{責任感|せきにんかん}→責任感：20441_sekininkan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{問|と}われる→問う：02299_tou⟧⟦{競技|きょうぎ}→競技：02606_kyougi⟧だ。
examples.english: Ekiden is a sport that tests your sense of responsibility in passing on the sash more than your individual speed.

notes:
The name comes from the Edo-period ⟦{駅|えき}→駅：02180_eki⟧ post stations where couriers changed horses. Instead of a baton, runners pass a cloth sash called a たすき.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{箱根|はこね}→箱根：30712_hakone⟧{駅伝|えきでん}: the Hakone Ekiden, run by university teams every January 2nd and 3rd
- {駅伝|えきでん}⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧: an ekiden meet
- たすき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つなぐ: to pass on the sash — also used figuratively for handing on a duty or tradition
- {駅伝|えきでん}⟦{選手|せんしゅ}→選手：03823_senshu⟧: an ekiden runner

CULTURAL NOTE:
Because each runner carries the team's hopes for one leg only, {駅伝|えきでん} is a stock metaphor in Japanese for teamwork across generations — a retiring employee may speak of passing the たすき to a successor.
